text: In 1954 a copy of Aristophanes's Lysistrata, consigned to a Beverly Hills book dealer, was intercepted by the U.S. Post Office as obscene and returned only after a suit aided by the ACLU; the year is approximate. In 1967 the military clique then ruling Greece banned a number of classic plays, among them Lysistrata, in Athens, presumably because of their independent and antiwar themes.
meta_description: Lysistrata by Aristophanes: intercepted by the U.S. Post Office as obscene around 1954, and banned in Athens in 1967 by Greece's ruling military clique.
changes: Two events from ban rows in date order; 1954 year hedged as approximate.
